record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
record.original_question: Let f:Y→B be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold to a smooth curve whose general fiber is a smooth surface. Fix an integer g>0. Is there a constant b(Y,g) such that every vertical curve C contained in a fiber, with geometric genus g, satisfies C^2 ≥ -b(Y,g), where self-intersection is computed inside the fiber containing C?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f: Y \to B$ be a surjective morphism from a smooth complex projective threefold $Y$ to a smooth projective curve $B$ such that the general fiber of $f$ is a smooth projective surface. Fix an integer $g > 0$. For a vertical curve $C \subset Y$ (i.e., an irreducible curve contained in some fiber $F = f^{-1}(b)$, $b \in B$) of geometric genus $g$, let $C^2$ denote the self-intersection of $C$ computed inside the (possibly singular or non-reduced) surface fiber $F$ containing it.

Question: Does there exist a constant $b(Y, g)$, depending only on $Y$ and $g$, such that
$$C^2 \geq -b(Y, g)$$
for every vertical curve $C \subset Y$ of geometric genus $g$?
artifact.status_search_result: The bounded negativity conjecture, even for a single complex projective surface, remains open in general (known only in special cases such as surfaces with anticanonical Kodaira dimension ≥ 0 and some other settings). The fibered/family version asking for a uniform bound $b(Y,g)$ across all surface fibers of a threefold fibration is a strengthening that does not appear to have been resolved; recent literature on bounded negativity, Harbourne constants, and weighted variants treats it as an outstanding problem.

status_evidence.title: Negative curves on algebraic surfaces (Bauer et al., Duke Math. J.)
status_evidence.snippet: The Bounded Negativity Conjecture predicts that for every complex projective surface X there exists b(X) with C^2 ≥ -b(X) for all reduced curves C.
status_evidence.claim: The base conjecture for a single surface is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Bounded negativity, Harbourne constants and transversal arrangements of curves
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of Harbourne constants as quantitative refinements of the still-open bounded negativity conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats bounded negativity as an open problem with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Towards the weighted Bounded Negativity Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses progress toward weighted variants of the BNC.
status_evidence.claim: Variants of bounded negativity are active research with the conjecture not resolved.
